title: Advice needed - How do I convert this little game from 2d to 3d with scenery and graphics
author: GodzillaBorland
selftext:
I am trying to create some teasers for a chapter in my upcoming book. Claude acknowledges the story is worthy of a game but the 2D looks primitive.  
**The game** [Game ](https://theselfdrivingmind.com/Vijayanagara_Stage_1.html)  
Here is a decription from Claude:  
Vijayanagara Stage 1 is a carry-and-escape stealth game set during the fall of Vijayanagara. You play a temple attendant carrying Sri Namperumal — the deity idol — out of the temple through a corridor patrolled by guards, moving toward safety at the far end.

The core tension is the flame you carry. It has two states:

* **Open flame** — you move at full speed and can see, but guards spot you easily.
* **Cupped flame** — you're hidden in the dark, but you move slowly and see almost nothing.

So light is simultaneously your navigation tool and the thing that gets you caught. Every corridor stretch is a bet on which one you need more.

**What's built**

Guards have four states — patrol, suspicious, chase, and investigate — with vision cones that respect facing and line-of-sight, plus audio and visual tells so you can read their state before they read yours. If a guard reaches you, you're stunned rather than reset, so a mistake costs tempo instead of progress. Guards who lose you go investigate where they last saw you, which means running past and hiding isn't automatically safe.

The screen is under a darkness mask punched open by lamp light — guard lanterns, shrine lights, and moonlight throwing wall silhouettes. Shrines double as localStorage checkpoints, so closing the tab doesn't lose the run.

Also in: three difficulty levels, mobile joystick plus a CUP FLAME button, sound toggle, intro and outro story cards, and a READ SOURCE link out to the Substack piece in both the HUD and intro.

**Caveats**

Art is primitive shapes only — real sprites would be the single biggest visual upgrade. Portrait mobile still needs a camera zoom-out so the full corridor width fits on screen.
